entity: South Carolina Chapter of Trout Unlimited
stance_basis: letter explicitly requests delay of licensing and states project will have significant negative impacts on water quality and aquatic community
summary: The South Carolina Chapter of Trout Unlimited submitted detailed technical comments opposing the Bad Creek Pumped Storage Project, raising concerns about stream habitat destruction, siltation impacts on Howard Creek's trout fishery and spawning runs, degradation of Lake Jocassee's cold-water trout habitat, and inadequate flow augmentation mitigation. The organization argued that insufficient data existed to assess the project's full impacts and requested that licensing be deferred until ongoing studies were completed.
complaint_summary: The organization raises concerns about destruction of trout habitat in Bad and Howard Creeks, ongoing erosion from boring exploration sites, the significance of a newly documented spawning run of rainbow and brown trout in lower Howard Creek, and requests remedial erosion control and sufficient study time before licensing.

statement.text:
It is recognized throughout project documentation that approximately 2.3 miles of Fad and West Bad Creeks will be destroyed by impoundment and that some 3.5 miles of Howard Creek will be detraded as trout habitat for a number of years following construction. The addicant has stated that all measures will be taken to minimize siltation and to restore the stream to "prennject conditions" " on completion. Stalles are presently underway by the applicant to develop the base line information on present conditions. The assumption is made that the present condition of the drainage is indeed its true state or value to the area. The Howard Creek basin has in near memory been an excellent trout fishery. The construction of Hwy. 171 and 413 created major habitat impacts, although a reproductive eastern brook trout fishery still survives around 413. The intensive logging and associated road construction during the latter 1960's again impacted the basin. Recovery is being made at present in the Corbin and Limbersole basins with improving habitat. The Bad and Howard Creek basins, however, continue to be heavily impacted. The gross erosion from boring exploration sites in the basin is presently discharging to the stream. A photographic documentation of these sites was made January 10, 1976, and copies of photographs will be forwarded to FPC as they are available. Studies based on the present stream productivity cannot be considered indicative of the value of this stream fishery to the citizens of South Carolina.
